# text — provenance and attribution

Six minimal PDFs for Pass 4 (text extraction, ISO 32000-1 §9.10 and
§14.6/§14.8/§14.9), generated by `tools/gen-text-fixtures.py`, plus one
**render** fixture (`cidfonttype2-nocmap-embedded.pdf`, generated by
`tools/gen-cidfont-nocmap-fixtures.py`) documented in its own section
below. Each extraction file isolates **one** claim from the extraction
contract, so a failing test names the clause it broke rather than
reporting that "extraction is wrong".

## Source material and license (LEGAL.md §5)

**Nothing here derives from a third-party file.** These are `LEGAL.md`
§5 category (a): **wholly synthetic**, authored for this project,
generated byte by byte by a committed script
(`tools/gen-text-fixtures.py`) with no PDF library behind it. No
embedded font programs, no third-party CMap resources, no corpus
material — so no attribution is owed and none is claimed.

The absence of embedded font programs is worth stating explicitly,
because it is exactly what makes these fixtures cheap and legally
clean: **§9.10.2's ladder needs no font program for any of the rungs
pdfce implements.** Rung 1 reads a `/ToUnicode` CMap that lives inside
the PDF; rung 2 reads Annex D.2 tables and the Adobe Glyph List, both of
which `pdfce-core` already carries. A text-extraction fixture therefore
does not need a font, where a rendering fixture would.

Two of these files are consequently **not renderable** by
`pdfce-render` and are not meant to be: `identity-h-tounicode.pdf` and
`identity-h-no-tounicode.pdf` use `Identity-H` with a non-embedded
descendant, which §9.7.5.2 forbids and which `pdfce-render` correctly
refuses (`UnsupportedFont::CompositeNotEmbedded`). That extraction
succeeds on a file rendering rejects is the point, not an oversight: the
two directions are separate pipelines with separate requirements.

## Regenerating

```text
python tools/gen-text-fixtures.py
```

Deterministic — no timestamps, no `/ID`, no random values. Running it
twice produces byte-identical files, so these can be compared rather
than merely loaded. Requires nothing but a Python interpreter.

## The files

| File | The one thing it pins |
|---|---|
| `simple-winansi.pdf` | **§9.10.2 rung 2.** Standard-14 Helvetica with `/Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding` — the named-encoding disjunct of method 2's precondition, resolved through Annex D.2 → AGL. Also the two derived-whitespace cases: a `TJ` offset of −2000 opens an inter-word gap with **no space glyph anywhere** (S3/S4), and a second `Td` line exercises the derived line break (S5). |
| `identity-h-tounicode.pdf` | **§9.10.2 rung 1 on the modern shape.** `/Type0` + `/Identity-H` + `Adobe-Identity-0` + `/ToUnicode`. The CMap exercises all three §9.10.3 forms in one stream: a form-B `bfrange` (last-byte increment), a form-C array whose middle destination is a **three-code-point ligature** (one-to-many), and a form-A `bfchar` with a **surrogate pair** (U+2003E, the standard's own example value). One shown code (`<0099>`) is deliberately **outside** the CMap, so the documented per-code fallthrough has something to fall through on. |
| `identity-h-no-tounicode.pdf` | **The headline honesty metric.** The same font with `/ToUnicode` removed. §9.10.2 excludes `Identity-H` from rung 3's first disjunct *by name*, and an `Adobe-Identity-0` descendant satisfies neither half of the second — so the ladder has nothing left and every code must reach the failure clause and be counted. **A test that ever sees real text come out of this file has found a fabrication.** |
| `actual-text-drucker.pdf` | **§14.9.4's own EXAMPLE**, structurally verbatim: the glyphs read `Dru` / `k-` / `ker` with a `/Span << /ActualText (c) >>` covering the middle one, so the character content is `Drucker` — a German hyphenation that changes the spelling. Note the `'` operator sits *outside* the `EMC`; reading the example as if the sequence covered it too yields `Druc` and loses `ker`. |
| `artifact-and-reversed.pdf` | Two §14.8 mechanisms on one page. An `/Artifact` sequence with a full Table 330 property list (`/Type /Pagination /Subtype /Header /BBox`) around a running head, plus the bare `/Artifact BMC` form around a folio — classified, kept, and excluded from plain text by *policy* (A1/A3: no `shall` requires exclusion). And §14.8.2.3.3's own `ReversedChars` example, `( olleH )` then `( . dlrow )`, which "represents the text `Hello world .`" — the fixture that catches an implementation reversing the *sequence* instead of each *string*. |
| `tagged-marked.pdf` | The three document-level facts: `/MarkInfo << /Marked true /Suspects true >>` and a `/StructTreeRoot`, plus a `/TagSuspect << /TagSuspect /Ordering >>` region and a `/P << /MCID 0 >>` sequence. None of it changes a single extracted character — which is exactly why it needs a fixture of its own instead of being asserted incidentally somewhere else. |

## Uses

1. **Integration tests** — `crates/pdfce-core/tests/text_extract.rs`.
2. **Fuzz seed corpus** — the whole-file targets (`load_document`,
   `parse_object`, `text_extract`). Per decision 005 §6.5 fuzz seeds
   come from `fixtures/synthetic/` and never from a downloaded
   real-world PDF.
3. **CLI demonstration**:

   ```text
   pdfce-cli extract-text fixtures/synthetic/text/identity-h-tounicode.pdf
   pdfce-cli extract-text fixtures/synthetic/text/identity-h-no-tounicode.pdf --json
   ```

   The second must report `ladder_failures` equal to `codes_total` and
   name the font in its diagnostics.

## Render fixture — `cidfonttype2-nocmap-embedded.pdf`

Unlike the six extraction files above, this one **embeds a font
program** and exists to exercise the `pdfce-render` glyph-outline path,
not extraction. Generator: `tools/gen-cidfont-nocmap-fixtures.py`
(separate from `gen-text-fixtures.py`).

Still `LEGAL.md` §5 category (a) **wholly synthetic**: the embedded
TrueType is *built* by the generator with `fontTools.fontBuilder` from
glyph outlines defined in the script (a `.notdef` and one filled box) —
it contains **no third-party font data**, in particular none of the
Arial / Verdana / Century Gothic subsets from any real document. It is
an original, trivial, CC0 / public-domain synthetic font. Requires
`fonttools` (a dev-only tool dependency, not a pdfce runtime dependency)
to regenerate.

| File | The one thing it pins |
|---|---|
| `cidfonttype2-nocmap-embedded.pdf` | **The embedded-TrueType render class.** `/Type0` + `/Identity-H` + `/CIDFontType2` + embedded subset `FontFile2` + `/CIDToGIDMap`, and the embedded program has **no `cmap`** (legal per §9.7.4.2: selection is CID → GID via `/CIDToGIDMap`). The program uses sfnt version `0x00010000`, whose first byte is `0x00` (a PDF whitespace byte, Table 1). The page draws CID 1 → GID 1, a filled box. If the box paints, the glyf-by-GID path survived the format-detection whitespace-trim that once ate the sfnt magic's leading NUL and misrouted every embedded TrueType to the CFF parser. Pinned by `crates/pdfce-render/tests/cidfont_nocmap_render.rs`. |

Regenerate:

```text
python tools/gen-cidfont-nocmap-fixtures.py
```

Deterministic (no timestamps, no `/ID`); running it twice produces a
byte-identical file.
